title: Gesture-driven column stacking and incremental virtualization for large tables
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Problem: Our current virtualized table handles high row counts well but struggles with very wide tables (many columns) on narrow viewports. Users frequently need to scan groups of related columns and then collapse them to preserve space. Existing solutions (column pinning, responsive collapse) are either too static or require multiple clicks. We need a design that enables rapid, discoverable column compression/stacking driven by natural gestures and incremental rendering to keep memory/paint cost low.

Goals:
- Provide a gesture-driven way to compress groups of less-important columns into stacked summaries without losing scannability.
- Make transitions cheap by coupling UI gestures with incremental virtualization (render only visible column groups + their stacked summaries).
- Preserve keyboard and screen-reader accessibility; gestures must have equivalents (keyboard shortcuts and toolbar controls).
- Surface quick cell-level summaries (mini-aggregates) for stacked groups so users can still compare values at-a-glance.
- Capture telemetry around reflow/resize/stack events to inform heuristics for auto-compress.

Proposed approach:
1) Column stacking concept: allow the user to select a contiguous column range and invoke a stacking action via a two-finger horizontal swipe (touch/trackpad) or a sustained drag on the column gutter. The selected range collapses into a compact stacked cell that shows the top 3 values and an overflow indicator. Stacked state is reversible with the opposite gesture or via a small inline chip control.

2) Incremental virtualization: when columns are stacked, the renderer will treat the grouped columns as a single virtual column for layout/paint purposes. Only the visible rows' stacked summaries are rendered initially; detailed cells are lazily hydrated on hover or expand. This keeps memory and paint costs proportional to viewport complexity rather than total column count.

3) Gesture-based density switcher: incorporate a pinch-zoom gesture (trackpad/touch) over the table header to cycle density modes (comfortable / compact / dense). Each mode tweaks font-size, row-padding, and the threshold for when columns become eligible for auto-stacking. Provide a keyboard shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + =/-) and a persistent toolbar density menu for discoverability.

4) Mini-aggregates and summaries: stacked cells include one-line summaries (mean/median/count as configured by user), sparklines for numeric columns (optional), and a tooltip with the top N values. For mixed-type columns, a concise textual summary (e.g., "2 labels, 1 date") is shown.

5) Accessibility and keyboard flow: gestures have explicit equivalents: select columns via Shift+click or keyboard range selection, then press S to stack/unstack. Screen readers announce stacked groups as "collapsed group: columns A–D (3 visible rows summarized)" and expose an action to expand. Focus must move predictably into stacked cell controls.

6) Telemetry and heuristics: collect opt-in telemetry (user-configurable) about stacking frequency, auto-stack suggestions accepted/rejected, density changes, and latency/paint measurements during stack/unstack. Use this data to refine automatic suggestions for column stacking on similar datasets.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Complexity: gestures add discovery burden; we mitigate with initial onboarding overlay and explicit toolbar controls.
- Performance: incremental virtualization reduces paint cost but introduces complexity in hydration. We'll prototype a minimal hydration API so engineering can reuse existing cell renderers.
- Backwards compatibility: existing table APIs should remain functional; stacking will be an opt-in feature behind a feature flag.

Acceptance criteria:
- Users can stack and unstack column ranges using both gesture and keyboard/toolbar controls (end-to-end flow).
- Stacked groups render summaries for visible rows only; expanding a single row hydrates detailed cells without re-rendering the entire table.
- Density pinch gesture switches density reliably on supported devices and falls back to toolbar/keyboard on desktop.
- Screen readers correctly announce stacked groups and expose expand/collapse controls.
- Telemetry events emitted for stack/unstack and density changes and visible in Product analytics dashboard (basic event schema documented).

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity prototype (Figma) showing gestures, stacked cell visual states, and density transitions.
- Interaction spec complete with keyboard equivalents, ARIA notes, and animation durations.
- Engineering API proposal for incremental hydration and virtual column grouping.
- Small lab usability test (n=6) with participants from Support and Solutions to validate discoverability.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: complete prototype and interaction spec.
- Week 2: engineering spike to validate hydration approach and perf benchmark.
- Week 3: iterate design based on spike and run small usability sessions.
- Week 4: soft launch behind feature flag to internal users with telemetry enabled.

Links to artifacts: Figma: https://redwood.design/figma/table-stacking-proto (placeholder), Spike doc: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/eng/table-stacking-spike (placeholder), GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/182 (placeholder).
